title: CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCING PHILOSOPHY
content:
👋 ሰላም፤ ጤና ይስጥልን ውድ የEthioFresh ተማሪዎች! እንኳን ወደ logic and critical thinking ኮርስ በሰላም መጣችሁ። ዛሬ የChapter 1 የመጀመሪያውን ክፍል በደንብ ዘንጣችሁ እንድትረዱትና ለፈተና 100% ዝግጁ እንድትሆኑ አድርገን በስፋት ይዘንላችሁ መጥተናል። በዚህ ክፍል የPhilosophy ትርጉም፣ Etymology፣ አጠቃላይ ባህሪያት (Features) እና የ'Having' እና 'Doing' philosophy ልዩነቶችን በዝርዝር እንመለከታለን። እስከ መጨረሻው አብራችሁን ቆዩ!👇👇👇


Lesson 1: Meaning and Nature of Philosophy

Introduction and the Definition Problem
Because of its universal nature, it is difficult to define philosophy in terms of a specific subject matter. It may be easy to define other disciplines, such as chemistry, physics, or geography, in terms of a subject matter because they have their own specific subject matters to primarily deal with. However, it is difficult to do the same with philosophy, because philosophy has no specific subject matter to deal with primarily. Philosophy deals primarily with issues, which are universal in nature. However, this should not lead us into thinking that philosophy is incomprehensible. It is only to say that whenever you want to understand philosophy, it is better to read different thoughts of philosophers, consciously see its salient features by yourself, participate in it, and do it.

Philosophy is not as elusive as it is often thought to be, nor is it remote from our various problems. It is unanimously agreed that the best way to learn and understand philosophy is to philosophize; i.e., to be confronted with philosophical questions, to use philosophical language, to become acquainted with differing philosophical positions and maneuvers, to read the philosophers themselves, and to grapple with the issues for oneself. Socrates once stated that “Wonder is the feeling of a philosopher, and philosophy begins in wonder.” Most of us may not have clear knowledge about the history, nature, language, and issues of philosophy, but we all think and reflect in our own way about issues that matter to us most. We are all touched and moved by the feelings of wonder from which all philosophy derives. Thus, we all participate, more or less, in philosophical issues, even though thinking alone cannot make us philosophers.

👉 • ለምን ፍልስፍናን እንደ Chemistry ወይም Physics በግልጽ መተርጎም ከበደ? : Chemistry ስለ chemicals፣ Physics ስለ matter/energy በግልጽ የተወሰነ ርዕስ (specific subject matter) አላቸው። Philosophy ግን የተወሰነ ወሰን የለውም፤ ሁለንተናዊ የሆኑ ጉዳዮችን (universal issues) ነው የሚያጠናው።
• ፍልስፍናን ለመረዳት ከሁሉ የተሻለው መንገድ : ንድፈ-ሀሳብ በቃል መሸምደድ ሳይሆን Philosophize ማድረግ (በፍልስፍናዊ ጥያቄዎች ላይ መመራመር፣ ማሰብ እና መከራከር) ነው። ሶቅራጥስ እንደተናገረው ፍልስፍና የሚጀምረው ከWonder (በነገሮች መደነቅና ጥያቄ ከማንሳት) ነው።
• (ወንድሜ/እህቴ... "Philosophy ይከብዳል" ብለህ እንዳታስብ! የጓደኛህን ስልክ password ለመገመት ስትጨነቅ እንደነበረው ሁሉ፣ አሁንም ህይወት ላይ ጥያቄ ካነሳህ በትንሹም ቢሆን philosophize እያደረግክ ነው ማለት ነው! 😄)


Etymological Definition of Philosophy
Etymologically, the word “philosophy” comes from two Greek words: “philo” and “sophia”, which mean “love” and “wisdom”, respectively. Thus, the literal definition of philosophy is “love of wisdom”. The ancient Greek thinker Pythagoras was the first to use the word “philosopher” to call a person who clearly shows a marked curiosity in the things he experiences. Anyone who raises questions such as Does God exist? What is reality? What is the ultimate source of Being? What is knowledge? What does it mean to know? How do we come to know? What is value? is showing a curiosity that can be described as a vital concern for becoming wise about the phenomena of the world and human experiences. Seeking wisdom is among the various essences of philosophy, but this is not sufficient by itself to understand philosophy, for not all wisdom is philosophy.

👉 የቃሉ አመጣጥ (Etymological Definition) :
• Philosophy የሚለው ቃል የመጣው ከሁለት የግሪክ ቃላት ነው፡ Philo (ፍቅር / Love) እና Sophia (ጥበብ / Wisdom)። ስለዚህ በቀጥታ ሲተረጎም "Love of Wisdom" (የጥበብ ፍቅር) ማለት ነው።
• Pythagoras የመጀመሪያው ራሱን "Philosopher" ብሎ የጠራ ሰው ነው። እንደ "አምላክ አለ? እውቀት ምንድን ነው?" ያሉ ጥያቄዎችን የሚያነሳ ሰው ሁሉ የጥበብ ፍላጎት እንዳለው ያሳያል።


Socratic Understanding of Wisdom and Philosophy
The wisdom that philosophers seek is not the wisdom of expert technical skills or professional knowledge. Someone may be encyclopedic and seemingly intelligent, but actually foolish when it comes to understanding the meaning and significance of what he knows. According to Socrates, wisdom consists of a critical habit, eternal vigilance about all things, and a reverence for truth, whatever its form and wherever its place. Based on the Socratic understanding of wisdom, philosophy, as a pursuit of wisdom, is the development of critical habits, the continuous search for truth, and the questioning of the apparent.

To interrogate the obvious means to deal creatively with the phenomenal world, to go beyond common understanding, and to speculate about things that other people accept without doubt. However, questioning/criticism is not the final end of philosophy, though raising the right question is often taken as its essence and direction. As Vincent Barry stated, the philosophical enterprise is “an active imaginative process of formulating proper questions and resolving them by rigorous, persistent analysis.”

Philosophy is a rational and critical enterprise that tries to formulate and answer fundamental questions through an intensive application of reason—an application that draws on analysis, comparison, and evaluation. It has two main sides:
• Constructive side: It attempts to formulate rationally defensible answers to fundamental questions concerning reality, value, knowledge, and truth.
• Critical side: It deals with giving rational critique, analysis, clarification, and evaluation of answers given to basic metaphysical, epistemological, and axiological questions.

Philosophy is an activity, not merely a theory to be memorized. A philosopher is great not because he mastered philosophy, but because he did it—through an extraordinary ability to critically think, conceptualize, analyze, compare, evaluate, and understand.

👉 • ጥበብ (Wisdom) ሲባል ምን ማለት ነው? : በሶክራጥስ እይታ ጥበብ ማለት የቴክኒክ ክህሎት ወይም ብዙ መረጃ በጭንቅላት መያዝ (encyclopedic መሆን) አይደለም። ጥበብ ማለት ተችነት (Critical habit)፣ ለዕውነት ሁልጊዜ ንቁ መሆን እና የሚታዩትን ነገሮች መጠራጠርና መመርመር ነው።
• ሁለቱ የፍልስፍና ገፅታዎች (Two Sides of Philosophy) :
1. Constructive Side (ገንቢ ገፅታ): ለዋና ዋና ጥያቄዎች በምክንያት የተደገፉ አዳዲስ መልሶችን ያዘጋጃል።
2. Critical Side (ተች/መሪማሪ ገፅታ): የተሰጡ መልሶችን ይመረምራል፣ ይተቻል፣ ያጠራል።

💡 Exam Hint: ፈተና ላይ "What makes someone a great philosopher?" ተብሎ ቢጠየቅ፡ መልሱ የፍልስፍና ቲዎሪዎችን በቃል መሸምደዱ ሳይሆን "His/her ability to philosophize" (የመመራመር፣ የመተቸትና የመተንተን አቅሙ) ነው!


Lesson 2: Basic Features of Philosophy

As an academic discipline, philosophy has its own salient features that distinguish it from other academic disciplines. The general features of philosophy can be summarized into 5 key points:

1. Philosophy as a set of views/beliefs vs. A process of reflection ("Having" vs "Doing")
• Informal Sense ("Having" a philosophy): Refers to a set of views or beliefs about life and the universe, often held uncritically. When a person says “my philosophy is...”, they refer to an informal personal attitude.
• Formal Sense ("Doing" philosophy): Philosophy is a process of reflecting on and criticizing our most deeply held conceptions and beliefs. "Having" a philosophy is necessary for "doing" philosophy, but it is not sufficient on its own. A genuine philosophical attitude is searching, critical, open-minded, and tolerant.

Why Philosophers Disagree:
Philosophers take a second look at common-sense materials and try to face life's problems impartially. They often disagree due to three main reasons:
1. They view things from different points of view, with different assumptions, personal experiences, and cultural backgrounds.
2. They live in a changing universe where people, society, and nature continuously change.
3. They deal with areas of human experience where evidence is incomplete, leading to different interpretations.

2. Philosophy is a rational attempt to look at the world as a whole
Philosophy seeks to combine the conclusions of various sciences and human experiences into a consistent worldview. Unlike a scientist, businessperson, or artist who has a specialized slant, a philosopher seeks an overall view of life as a totality.

3. Logical analysis of language and clarification of concepts
A major function of philosophy is analyzing language and clarifying the meaning of words/terms to expose confusion and nonsense in science and everyday affairs.

4. Philosophy is a group of perennial problems
Philosophy presses inquiry into the deepest fundamental questions of human existence (e.g., What is truth? What is justice? Is there life after death? Does God exist?). These persistent questions give rise to major systems of thought like Idealism, Realism, Pragmatism, and Existentialism.

👉 • "Having" vs "Doing" Philosophy: "Having a philosophy" ማለት ዝም ብሎ የግል አመለካከት ወይም እምነት መያዝ ነው (Informal)። "Doing philosophy" ማለት ደግሞ እምነቶቻችንን በምክንያት መመርመርና መተቸት ነው (Formal)።
• ለምን Philosophers ይለያያሉ/ይከራከራሉ? : በ 3 ዋና ምክንያቶች፡ 1) የተለያየ ልምድና ባህል ስላላቸው፣ 2) አለም ሁልጊዜ ተለዋዋጭ ስለሆነች፣ እና 3) የተሟላ መረጃ (complete evidence) በሌለባቸው ርዕሶች ላይ ስለሚያጠኑ።
• አለምን በሙሉነት ማየት (Look at the world as a whole): እንደ ሌሎች ሳይንሶች የተወሰነ ክፍል ላይ ብቻ አያተኩርም፤ ሙሉ ህይወትንና አለምን አጣጥሞ ያያል።
• የቋንቋና የቃላት ትርጉምን ማጠራት (Logical analysis of language): ብዥታዎችን ለማስወገድ ቃላትንና ፅንሰ-ሀሳቦችን ይተነትናል።

💡 Exam Hint: በፈተና ላይ "Which of the following is true about 'Having' and 'Doing' philosophy?" ከተባለ፡ "Having a philosophy is necessary but NOT sufficient for doing philosophy" የሚለውን አትርሱ!


📝 Practice Exam Questions

1. Etymologically, the word "Philosophy" literally means:
A) Search for knowledge
B) Love of wisdom
C) Critical thinking
D) Scientific analysis
Answer: B | Explanation: It derives from Greek "philo" (love) and "sophia" (wisdom).

2. According to Socrates, wisdom primarily consists of:
A) Having encyclopedic memory of facts
B) Developing critical habits and continuous search for truth
C) Mastering technical skills of a profession
D) Accepting common sense without questioning
Answer: B | Explanation: Socrates argued that wisdom is not just information storage, but eternal vigilance and critical habits.

3. Which of the following is NOT a reason why philosophers disagree with one another?
A) They view things from different points of view and cultural backgrounds.
B) They live in a constantly changing universe.
C) Philosophy only uses scientific laboratory experiments to prove facts.
D) They deal with human experiences where evidence is incomplete.
Answer: C | Explanation: Philosophy deals with universal issues and reason, not just restricted lab experiments.
